title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The UK government has responded to the Committee’s 2020 report on artificial intelligence and public standards, outlining its plans for how the sector should be regulated and guided. It stresses creating clear rules, ethical guidelines and working with industry to ensure AI is safe, trustworthy and in the public interest.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual has set out a plan for how it will oversee the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector, aiming to keep testing fair, reliable, and transparent. The policy was released at the request of the Secretary of State for Education, Science, Innovation and Technology, and Business and Trade, showing that the government wants clear rules around AI in exams.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report investigates how copyright law applies when AI systems are trained on copyrighted works and assesses the legal, economic, and ethical impact of this practice. It provides recommendations to balance creators’ rights with the need for innovation in AI development.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government has issued a response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence, addressing the report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’. It outlines plans to strengthen AI regulation, promote ethical development, and support innovation while ensuring public safety and transparency.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document explains why a committee has been formed to review how artificial intelligence should meet public standards, outlining its goals, scope, and key responsibilities. It also offers a set of FAQs to help people understand the committee’s review process and what to expect.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the UK Science and Technology Committee, addressing the governance of artificial intelligence. The submission outlines the organisation’s perspectives and recommendations on AI policy and oversight to guide the committee’s inquiry.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy explains how the growing use of artificial intelligence will change the rules and oversight for medical products, from development to market approval. It outlines concrete steps to apply the AI White Paper’s principles—such as transparency, safety, and accountability—to ensure that AI‑enabled medical products are regulated responsibly and effectively.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence AI Strategy aims to make the organisation the leading AI‑capable defence entity among similarly sized forces, prioritising effectiveness, efficiency, trust and influence. It outlines how to harness AI technologies to support operations and maintain strategic advantage.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to make the most of AI’s benefits. It also outlines steps to identify, monitor and manage any risks that AI might bring to transport services.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report reviews how copyright‑protected works are being used to train and develop AI systems under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It summarizes progress, outlines challenges, and offers recommendations for balancing AI innovation with copyright rights.
